weeks: 5-8 (runs parallel to blocks B and D; gated on the week 1-2 perception block, not on grammar). ~20-25 min/day inside the 90-100 min budget. 175 items, ~9 new items/day.

items.note: 2 morae: sa-N. The N is a full beat.
wago. This is the form you say when counting or when nothing forces shi.
2 morae: kyu-u. kyu is ONE mora (yoon), the second u is the second beat.
2 morae. Never *ju.
Survives only in fixed slots: shigatsu, shichi. Never volunteer it for a count.
Obligatory in shichiji, shichigatsu. Easily misheard as ichi on the phone; ree-tokens and nana exist because of this.
Obligatory in kuji, kugatsu. Never *kyuuji, never *kyuugatsu.
NOT rei. Two beats, both /e/.

items.romaji: ichi ni san yon go roku nana hachi kyuu juu
items.audioText: ichi ni san yon go roku nana hachi kyuu juu
items.note: Run against a beat. ichi/roku/hachi are 2 morae with a short vowel; san/kyuu/juu are 2 morae with a special mora. Ten even beats, no rushing.

items.romaji: juu kyuu hachi nana roku go yon san ni ichi
items.audioText: juu kyuu hachi nana roku go yon san ni ichi
items.note: Backwards is the real test that the digits are individually retrievable and not one memorised ribbon.

items.romaji: ichi ni san shi go roku shichi hachi ku juu
items.audioText: ichi ni san shi go roku shichi hachi ku juu
items.note: RECOG only. You will hear this one; you say chant 16.
Additive: juu + digit. No sound change anywhere in 11-19.
juushi exists but is avoided; say juuyon.
Multiplicative: digit + juu. 20-90 is one clean pattern with zero exceptions.
Never *shijuu in modern counting.
Exemplar: tens then units, no linker. 99 = kyuujuukyuu.
hya is ONE mora. hyaku = 2 morae, not 3. Never *ichihyaku.
Nasal-triggered voicing: N + hy -> by. Same phonology as sanbon, sanbiki, sanbai.
Obstruent-triggered gemination: roku + hyaku -> roppyaku. 4 morae: ro-Q-pya-ku.
hachi + hyaku -> happyaku. 4 morae: ha-Q-pya-ku.
Never *ichisen for a bare 1000 (ichisen appears only inside larger numbers).
N + s -> z. Same nasal voicing as sanbyaku, different consonant.
hachi + sen -> hassen. Geminate ss, 4 morae: ha-Q-se-N. Contrast happyaku.
THE MYRIAD BREAK. Japanese regroups every FOUR digits, not three. 10,000 is ichiman, never *juusen. And the ichi is obligatory: never bare *man. 100,000 = juuman, 1,000,000 = hyakuman.
hito-/futa- is the same wago pair as hitori/futari.
Geminate. mi + tsu -> mittsu. 3 morae: mi-Q-tsu.
NO geminate here. itsutsu, not *ittsu. The odd one out in the run mittsu-yottsu-itsutsu-muttsu.
No geminate.
5 morae. The longest counter word you will meet; do not clip it.
Breaks the series: NOT *tootsu, NOT *tokoo. Two morae, one long o. Past ten the -tsu series stops and you switch to juu + a real counter.

items.romaji: hitotsu futatsu mittsu yottsu itsutsu muttsu nanatsu yattsu kokonotsu too
items.audioText: hitotsu futatsu mittsu yottsu itsutsu muttsu nanatsu yattsu kokonotsu too
items.note: THE ESCAPE HATCH. -tsu counts almost any concrete inanimate thing up to ten. Owning this chant makes the entire counter tail droppable: if you cannot retrieve -ko, -hon or -mai in time, say the -tsu form and you are still correct-sounding.
Also means 'alone'.
4 morae: sa-N-ni-N. Two separate nasal beats; do not merge them.
THE REAL IRREGULAR. yo-nin, 3 morae. NOT *yonnin, NOT *yonin with a doubled n. Compare yoji, which drops the n the same way.
No gemination: -nin does not trigger it. rokunin, not *rokunnin.
4 morae: na-N-ni-N.
ichi + ko -> ikko. Geminate.
No voicing: -ko starts with k, which the nasal does not voice here. sanko, not *sango.
roku + ko -> rokko.
ichi + hon -> ippon. 4 morae: i-Q-po-N.
MINIMAL PAIR WITH ACCENT ONLY: nihon [1] = two bottles; Nihon [2] = Japan. Same segments, different drop. This is why accent is on every card.
N + h -> b.
Stays h. yon does not trigger voicing even though it ends in n.
roku + hon -> roppon.
-mai is the easy series: NO sound changes at all in 1-10. Use it as the rest cell.
rokumai, NOT *rokkumai. -mai never geminates.
Same p/b/h alternation as -hon, on a different base.
Third instance of the same p/b/h series. Once -hon is automatic, -hiki and -hai cost almost nothing.
Homophone with sanbai 'threefold' [0]; they differ by accent. Keep 'threefold' out of the deck for now.
THE ONE FLOOR IRREGULAR: N + k -> g. sangai, not *sankai. Everything else in the floor series keeps k.
THE PAYOFF CONTRAST: sangai = 3rd floor, sankai = 3 times. Identical except the g/k, and that one consonant is the whole meaning.
Fully homophonous with rokkai '6th floor'. Context alone disambiguates - which is fine, and worth saying out loud so it stops feeling like a mistake.
Assembly exemplar: hundreds, then tens, then -en, no pauses and no linkers.
SYLLABIC N BEFORE A VOWEL: written sen'en, four morae se-N-e-N. The N is its own beat and does NOT slur into the e. *senen would be three morae and wrong.
Again n' before a vowel. 6 morae: i-chi-ma-N-e-N. The commonest banknote; you will hear it constantly.
LEXICALIZED EXCEPTION: yo-ji, never *yonji and never *shiji. Same yo- as in yonin.
No gemination: rokuji, not *rokkuji.
LEXICALIZED EXCEPTION: the shichi form is required. *nanaji is not said (nanaji is heard occasionally for clarity but do not produce it).
LEXICALIZED EXCEPTION: ku-ji, never *kyuuji. Two morae only.
-fun/-pun is the fourth p/b/h-type series, and the busiest one.
N + f -> p here, NOT b. Contrast sanbon/sanbiki/sanbai, which do voice. -fun is the one that geminates the nasal into p.
The single most useful minute word: clock faces are read in fives.
jippun also exists and is older/formal; juppun is what you say and mostly what you hear.
Goes AFTER the hour: sanji han. Two morae, ha-N.
Goes BEFORE the hour: gozen juuji. The opposite side from han.
made = the whole stretch up to then. made ni = at some point before then. goji made hatarakimasu vs goji made ni onegaishimasu.
-me turns a count into a position. Built straight off the -tsu series you already own.
-banme is the general ordinal, usable where -tsume is not.
Totally unrelated to hitotsu. Must be memorised whole. 5 morae: tsu-i-ta-chi.
Geminate. Compare mittsu: same mi- root, different tail.
yo- again, as in yoji and yonin. Never *yonka.
Homophone with itsuka 'someday' [1] - the accent differs. Date sense stays in a date frame for now.
NO geminate, unlike mikka/yokka. mu-i-ka, 3 morae.
LENGTH IS THE WHOLE CONTRAST: yooka (8th) vs yokka (4th). Long vowel versus geminate, and nothing else. Drill this pair to death.
Built on too. Contrast tooka / yooka / yokka as a three-way length-and-gemination set.
The yo- irregular survives inside the teens. Never *juuyonnichi.
The last wago date. From 21 on it is regular: nijuuichinichi.
Regular exemplar: number + nichi. Everything outside the twelve wago dates works this way.
5 morae, long oo. Never -yobi.
n' BEFORE y: ki-N-yo-o-bi, 5 morae. Not *kinyoobi with a palatal nyo - the N is its own beat.
n' before y again.
Months are just number + gatsu. Only three cells misbehave: 4, 7, 9.
LEXICALIZED: shi-, never *yongatsu. Note this is shi, NOT the yo- used by yoji/yonin/yokka - the exceptions do not all pick the same alternate.
LEXICALIZED: never *nanagatsu.
LEXICALIZED: ku-, never *kyuugatsu. Same ku as kuji.
2 morae: kyo-o. kyo is one mora. NOT kyou.
3 morae: ki-no-o.
Geminate. 4 morae: a-sa-Q-te.
4 morae: ra-i-shu-u.
SIX morae: i-Q-shu-u-ka-N. Geminate, then a long vowel, then a moraic N. The heaviest word in this block - say it slow and full before you ever say it fast.
The o drops in casual shop speech. kore o kudasai is the full form; kore kudasai is what is said.
Softer and wider than kudasai. Works on its own as a whole turn.
The buying-time filler. Learn it early: it is what keeps a slow number from sounding like a breakdown. Long ee, two beats.
Marks the decision point in a transaction.
What you say handing over cash or a card.
RECOG ONLY - the clerk says it, you answer hai or daijoobu desu. You will hear this at every register.
5 morae: re-shi-i-to. The long ii is a full extra beat.
Precedes the total: zenbu de sen'en desu.

sentences.gloss: That one over there is a thousand yen.
sentences.note: Listen for the N beat before the e. sen'en is four beats, not three.
The one cell in the run with no geminate. Feel the difference against yottsu on the card before it.
Two beats. A clipped *to is a different word entirely.
What you answer at a restaurant door.
Three beats. If you hear four in your own mouth you have said *yonnin.
Contrast card 23: ippai is a glassful, ippon is the bottle.
nihon [1], not Nihon [2]. The drop is the only thing keeping you from asking for two Japans.

sentences.gloss: The shop is on the second floor.
The restaurant is on the third floor.
sentences.note: The g is the whole point. *sankai here means 'three times'.
Play back-to-back with card 39 in the same session. Same word shape, one consonant apart, two unrelated meanings.
Two beats. *yonji does not exist.

sentences.gloss: The shop is open until nine.

sentences.note: p, not b. Say sanbon and sanpun back to back and hear that they do not rhyme.
THE RULE: ni attaches to times you could point to on a calendar or a clock face. sanji ni, getsuyoobi ni, tsuitachi ni.
NO ni. kyoo means 'today' only relative to the moment you speak - it is deictic, so it takes no particle. Never *kyoo ni.
Bare again. Same reason as kyoo.
Weekday takes ni; kyoo does not. Put cards 58 and 65 in the same review run so the contrast is felt, not memorised.

sentences.gloss: What day of the week is it?

sentences.note: Immediately after card 69. Long vowel versus geminate: yooka / yokka. If you cannot hear it here, go back to the week 1-2 length drills for one session.
Order is big-to-small, always: month then day.
The single most useful sentence in this block for finding anything on foot.
Practise stalling on purpose. A filled pause is fluent; a silent one is not.

sentences.gloss: In that case, I'll take this.

sentences.note: RECOG only. You answer hai or iie - never produce this one.

sentences.gloss: That's a thousand yen in total.
sentences.note: The clerk's line. Recognising zenbu de tells you the total is arriving next - that half-second of warning is what makes the number catchable.

drills.name: Two-second dictation: 30 quantities, times and dates
drills.target: 27 of 30 correct, each answer begun within 2.0 s of the audio ending. Run daily from W5D3; the block is not finished until this is passed twice on consecutive days.
drills.spec:
Audio plays ONE item at a time. Learner says the English back aloud within 2 s (a stopwatch beep at 2.0 s marks the deadline; an answer that starts after the beep is wrong even if correct). No replays, no pausing. Score aloud, move on. Full set, in the order run:
1. audio 'sanbon' -> 'three (bottles)'
2. 'sanbai' -> 'three glasses'
3. 'sanbiki' -> 'three animals'
4. 'sanpun' -> 'three minutes'
5. 'sanmai' -> 'three flat things'
6. 'sangai' -> 'third floor'
7. 'sankai' -> 'three times'
8. 'sannin' -> 'three people'
9. 'mittsu' -> 'three (things)'
10. 'roppon' -> 'six (bottles)'
11. 'rokunin' -> 'six people'
12. 'rokuji' -> 'six o'clock'
13. 'roppun' -> 'six minutes'
14. 'rokko' -> 'six pieces'
15. 'yoji' -> 'four o'clock'
16. 'yonin' -> 'four people'
17. 'yokka' -> 'the 4th'
18. 'yooka' -> 'the 8th'
19. 'tooka' -> 'the 10th'
20. 'juuyokka' -> 'the 14th'
21. 'hatsuka' -> 'the 20th'
22. 'tsuitachi' -> 'the 1st'
23. 'kuji han' -> 'half past nine'
24. 'gozen juuji' -> 'ten a.m.'
25. 'gogo shichiji juugofun' -> 'seven fifteen p.m.'
26. 'sen'en' -> 'one thousand yen'
27. 'ichiman'en' -> 'ten thousand yen'
28. 'roppyaku' -> 'six hundred'
29. 'happyaku' -> 'eight hundred'
30. 'hyakugojuuen' -> 'one hundred fifty yen'
Items 1-8 are deliberately one minimal set: the same numeral against eight counters. If a miss happens, it will happen there, and that is the diagnostic.

drills.name: Reverse dictation: English in, Japanese out
drills.target: 25 of 30 within 2.0 s. Run it only after the RECOG version is passing.
drills.spec: Same 30 items, direction flipped. English prompt, learner produces the Japanese aloud, native audio plays to check. E.g. prompt 'six minutes' -> say 'roppun' -> audio 'roppun'. Prompt 'the 8th' -> 'yooka' -> audio 'yooka'. Prompt 'four o'clock' -> 'yoji' -> audio 'yoji'. Prompt 'ten thousand yen' -> 'ichiman'en' -> audio 'ichiman'en'. A hesitation past 2 s counts as a miss even if the word is right - the whole point of this block is retrieval speed at conversational tempo.

drills.name: The p/b/h chant
drills.target: Run all four series without a stumble at 100 bpm, one cell per beat. No grading, no scoring - it is a rhythm exercise.
drills.spec:
Four series, same phonology, run one after another against a metronome:
-hon: 'ippon nihon sanbon yonhon gohon roppon' | 'nanbon'
-hiki: 'ippiki nihiki sanbiki yonhiki gohiki roppiki' | 'nanbiki'
-hai: 'ippai nihai sanbai yonhai gohai roppai' | 'nanbai'
-fun: 'ippun nifun sanpun yonpun gofun roppun' | 'nanpun'
The shape is identical every time: 1 geminates, 3 changes at the nasal, 6 geminates, 4 and 5 do nothing. The one thing to notice out loud: the first three series voice at 3 (b), and -fun does not (sanpun, p). Say 'sanbon sanbiki sanbai SANPUN' as a tag at the end of every run until the odd one is felt rather than recalled.

drills.name: The escape hatch
drills.target: Under pressure, produce a usable -tsu form instead of freezing. Success is fluency, not counter accuracy.
drills.spec: Prompt with an object and a number; the learner must answer within 1.5 s using ANY correct counter. If the specific counter does not arrive in time, -tsu is the required fallback and scores as a pass. E.g. 'three apples' -> 'ringo o mittsu kudasai' (pass) or 'ringo o sanko kudasai' (also pass). 'two bottles of water' -> 'mizu o nihon kudasai' (pass) or 'mizu o futatsu kudasai' (pass). 'five tickets' -> 'kippu o gomai' (pass) or 'kippu o itsutsu' (pass). Freezing is the only fail. Run twenty items a session, mixed objects, numbers 1-9.

drills.name: The myriad ladder
drills.target: Say each rung without recomputing from English. The break at 10,000 must stop feeling like a break.
drills.spec: Ascending, then descending, said aloud: 'juu, hyaku, sen, ichiman' then 'juuman, hyakuman'. Then the prices: 'hyakuen, gohyakuen, sen'en, sanzen'en, ichiman'en'. Then the trap, said as an explicit self-correction: 'ten thousand is NOT juusen - ichiman'. English regroups at 1,000; Japanese regroups at 10,000, so every large number has to be re-cut, not translated digit by digit.

drills.name: Date irregular sweep
drills.target: All twelve wago dates in order, then in shuffled order, under 20 s.
drills.spec: In order: 'tsuitachi futsuka mikka yokka itsuka muika nanoka yooka kokonoka tooka juuyokka hatsuka'. Then shuffled prompts, English to Japanese: 'the 6th' -> 'muika', 'the 8th' -> 'yooka', 'the 3rd' -> 'mikka', 'the 1st' -> 'tsuitachi', 'the 20th' -> 'hatsuka', 'the 14th' -> 'juuyokka'. Then the length triad on its own, ten slow repetitions: 'yokka - yooka - tooka'.

drills.name: Transaction shadow
drills.target: Get through the whole exchange without a silent pause. ee to is allowed and encouraged.
drills.spec:
Recorded clerk audio, learner takes the customer turns aloud in real time:
clerk: 'irasshaimase' | learner: 'sumimasen, kore ikura desu ka'
clerk: 'sen'en desu' | learner: 'ee to... sore ja, kore kudasai'
clerk: 'fukuro irimasu ka' | learner: 'hai, onegaishimasu'
clerk: 'zenbu de sen'en desu' | learner: 'kore de onegaishimasu'
clerk: 'arigatoo gozaimashita' | learner: 'reshiito onegaishimasu'
Run three variants with different prices (hyakugojuuen, gohyakuen, ichiman'en) and different quantities so the frame stays live instead of becoming one memorised recording.

drills.name: Counter cell round-robin
drills.target: Any of the ~70 cells retrievable in under 1.5 s from a random prompt. This is the block's exit criterion alongside the dictation.
drills.spec: Random prompt of the form '<number> + <counter name>' in English, learner says the Japanese cell. E.g. 'six, animals' -> 'roppiki'. 'three, floors' -> 'sangai'. 'one, minutes' -> 'ippun'. 'four, people' -> 'yonin'. 'nine, o'clock' -> 'kuji'. 'six, flat' -> 'rokumai'. 'one, cups' -> 'ippai'. 'three, pieces' -> 'sanko'. Forty prompts a session, drawn evenly across the ten counters, cells 1-6 plus nan-.

lessons.title: Digits and the beat
lessons.drill: Chant 1-10 forward and back against a metronome. ichi/roku/hachi are two morae with short vowels; san/kyuu/juu are two morae with a special mora. Ten even beats.

lessons.title: The three-way alternation
lessons.drill: yon/shi, nana/shichi, kyuu/ku said as pairs. Flag now that the bound variants are not free choices: shichiji, kuji, shigatsu are fixed.

lessons.title: Prices, and the myriad break
lessons.drill: Myriad ladder. Dictation set items 26-30 only.

lessons.title: Buying one of something
lessons.drill: Transaction shadow, price hyakuen only.

lessons.title: The -tsu series, top half
lessons.drill: -tsu chant. Hold on itsutsu - it is the cell with no geminate, sitting between two that have one.

lessons.title: The -tsu series completed, and the escape hatch
lessons.drill: Escape hatch drill, first run. Say out loud what it buys you: any inanimate thing up to ten, always acceptable.

lessons.title: Counting people
lessons.drill: Round-robin, -nin only. yonin gets ten extra reps on its own - three beats, not four.

lessons.title: Tens and teens
lessons.drill: Count 11-99 by ones from 11-25, then by tens. Fourteen and seventeen use yon and nana.

lessons.title: Hundreds and thousands, with sound changes
lessons.drill: Myriad ladder plus the alternating cells alone: sanbyaku, roppyaku, happyaku, sanzen, hassen. Same two processes as the counters, met here first.

lessons.title: Glasses and cups: the p/b/h shape, first pass
lessons.drill: p/b/h chant, -hai line only.

lessons.title: Flat things (the easy series)
lessons.drill: Round-robin -mai. Deliberately restful: no sound changes anywhere. Use it to prove the alternations elsewhere are real and not just difficulty.

lessons.title: Long thin things, and one accent minimal pair
lessons.drill: p/b/h chant, -hon line. Then nihon [1] against Nihon [2], twenty alternations.

lessons.title: Animals and pieces
lessons.drill: p/b/h chant, all four lines for the first time, plus the sanbon/sanbiki/sanbai/SANPUN tag.

lessons.title: Floors and times: one consonant, two meanings
lessons.drill: sangai/sankai alternation, thirty reps. Then rokkai said twice with the two meanings named aloud - full homophony, and that is allowed.

lessons.title: Telling the hour
lessons.drill: Round-robin -ji. yoji, shichiji, kuji get triple weight: these three are the whole reason the alternation chant exists.

lessons.title: Minutes, a.m., p.m., half past
lessons.drill: Full 30-item dictation, first complete run. Expect the failure to land in items 1-8.

lessons.title: kara, made, made ni - and when time takes ni
lessons.drill: Sort twenty time expressions into takes-ni and takes-nothing. The rule to state plainly: a time you could point to on a calendar or clock face takes ni (sanji ni, getsuyoobi ni, tsuitachi ni); a time that only means anything relative to right now does not (kyoo, ashita, kinoo, raishuu). It is calendrical versus deictic, not arbitrary.

lessons.title: Today, tomorrow, and the days of the week
lessons.drill: Weekday chant. Hold kin'yoobi apart: ki-N-yo-o-bi, five beats, the N standing alone before the y. Then isshuukan said slowly six times - six morae, three different special morae in one word.

lessons.title: The date irregulars
lessons.drill: Date irregular sweep, both directions. Then the length triad yokka / yooka / tooka on its own for five minutes - this is the one place in the block where mishearing a beat changes the appointment.

lessons.title: Months, ordinals, and the whole transaction
lessons.drill: Transaction shadow, all three price variants. Then the full 30-item dictation for the exit check, followed by the reverse-direction version.
